description: Searches the Storika creator database on every search call; you do not name it and cannot turn it off. On a TikTok Shop campaign the creators come from TikTok Shop's affiliate marketplace and the creator database only fills in facts about them, so name no source; when the marketer asks for a keyword search, name tiktok_keyword with keywords, which runs alone in place of the marketplace, is charged, and shows whether TikTok Shop can reach each creator. It also searches the sources providers names or defaults to, and stores the creators found on the campaign: instagram_hashtag, tiktok_keyword, instagram_profile, instagram_post, instagram_mention, email_contacts, web and meta. instagram_hashtag reads live Instagram posts by hashtag and tiktok_keyword live TikTok videos by keyword; each is charged per call. instagram_mention scans who tagged or @mentioned the benchmark brands on Instagram and TikTok. email_contacts finds creators with a public contact email by topic, country, language and followers on Instagram and TikTok, and is charged per call. When email_contacts is among the sources, named or by default, the Storika creator database answers first with creators who have an email on file; email_contacts and later sources ask only for the rest, and email_contacts does not run when the database found them all. web reads the open web for creators that pages name and is charged per web pass, plus one lead read and one profile read. meta searches Meta's Instagram creator marketplace through the campaign brand's connected Instagram account by the first keyword, country and follower range, and is not charged. Countries and languages are musts when known; a creator with an unread value stays. Categories are hints; an unusable country or category is left out and named. The reply names the market each source searched, the search terms not sent, and the creators the follower range dropped. keep and drop with candidate ids record the marketer's calls on the shown list: with no intent it records them and searches nothing, intent more records them and searches again, and intent stop records them and freezes the final list. import_creator_list adds the brand's Google Sheets creator list in two calls with confirmation_ref, free. Example: platform "instagram", keywords ["sunscreen"].

benchmark_brand.description: One brand, the same as a one-entry benchmark_brands.

benchmark_brands.description: Up to 10 brands, each "@handle" or a name. Scans recent Instagram and TikTok posts that tag or @mention each brand. Takes instagram_mention as the only source and no keywords. Until the scan is done the reply says collecting, and a repeat call with the same arguments returns what it found.

brief.description: One or two sentences on the creators to find, in the operator own words: their topic, content style and audience. It holds no budget, dates or deliverables, because the search ranks creators by this text.

categories.description: Category hints, e.g. ["Beauty & Personal Care"]. They guide search terms and contact tags, and narrow the first creator database search. Unused names are reported.

confirmation_ref.description: From the import preview; works once.

countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes of countries the operator named, e.g. ["KR","US"] ("Korea" -> "KR"). A must outside the TikTok Shop marketplace: a creator known to be outside them is dropped, and one of unknown country stays. With none, the campaign country applies. Accepted codes: US, KR, JP, CA, GB, AU, FR, DE, IT, ES, NL, SE, NO, DK, FI, IE, CH, AT, BE, PT, PL, CZ, GR, TR, AE, SA, IL, IN, CN, TW, HK, SG, TH, VN, ID, PH, MY, BR, MX, AR, CL, CO, ZA, EG. At most 20.

drop.description: Candidate ids the marketer drops; they stay off this campaign.

anyOf.description: A candidate id this campaign's search returned.
A candidate id with the reason the marketer gave.

candidate_id.description: A candidate id this campaign's search returned.

reason.description: The marketer's reason, in their own words.

reason_code.description: For a drop, the listed reason that fits best.

exclude_handles.description: Handles of creators the operator turned down. The search leaves them out.

feedback.description: The marketer's own words about the creators shown, such as what to find more or less of. It is saved for the campaign, and every later search of it reads it. A rule the marketer gives for every later search or outreach message belongs in the Learned Facts of CAMPAIGN.md or BRAND.md, not here.

followers_max.description: Drop creators above this follower count.

followers_min.description: Drop creators below this follower count.

import_creator_list.description: Previews the brand's Google Sheets creator list; send confirmation_ref next to add it.

intent.description: more: write the marks, then search again. stop: write the marks, then freeze the final list. With keep, drop or feedback and no intent, they are written and nothing is searched or charged.

anyOf.description: A candidate id this campaign's search returned.
A candidate id with the reason the marketer gave.

candidate_id.description: A candidate id this campaign's search returned.

reason.description: The marketer's reason, in their own words.

reason_code.description: For a drop, the listed reason that fits best.

keywords.description: Search words, used as post words and topic hashtags. The live search sends the first 5; the reply counts the rest.

languages.description: ISO 639-1 codes, e.g. ["ko","en"]. Must: drop known mismatches; keep unknown. Convert names ("English" -> "en"). At most 20.

platform.description: The campaign's platform, or the one the operator named when the campaign runs on both. A search and intent more need it.

providers.description: Sources to search in order, each once: instagram_hashtag reads live Instagram posts by hashtag, tiktok_keyword live TikTok videos by keyword, instagram_profile reads named Instagram profiles, instagram_post reads named Instagram posts, instagram_mention scans who tagged or @mentioned the benchmark_brands, email_contacts finds creators with a public contact email by topic, country, language and followers, web creators the open web names, meta Meta's Instagram creator marketplace for the campaign brand. instagram_hashtag, tiktok_keyword, instagram_profile and instagram_post read only the platform in their name. Left out, it runs the platform's live search, after email_contacts on a call with a follower range, countries or languages; named sources replace these. A TikTok Shop campaign leaves it out to search TikTok Shop's affiliate marketplace; tiktok_keyword with keywords runs there alone, in place of the marketplace.

request_id.description: A new id for each search; send the same id to retry without a second charge. A search and intent more need it.

requested_count.description: How many creators to find: the whole number the operator stated, at least 1, passed as stated even above 100. One search finds at most 100, so a larger ask runs as 100 and the answer says more takes further searches. The outside sources return at most this many creators. Omit it when the operator named no number: the search then finds 20 creators, or fewer when less of the campaign's recommendation is left.

source_inputs.description: Inputs for the sources named in providers, one key per source. A key for a source not named in providers is refused. storika_database cannot be named: it reads the brief and always runs first, and with no brief or keywords it does not search.

email_contacts.description: Takes keywords, categories, countries, languages and the follower range. Returns each creator's handle, followers and the kinds of contact they state. Price: charged per search, never above its line. Usually under a minute, inside this call.

similar_to.description: A creator handle or profile link; finds creators like them.

instagram_hashtag.description: Takes hashtags, or the keywords when hashtags is left out. Returns each creator's handle, post links and captions. It reads no bio or links, so bio_status says not_read; instagram_profile reads them, charged as its own source. Price: charged per creator requested, once it finds any creator. Usually 1 to 4 minutes, in the background.

instagram_mention.description: Takes benchmark_brands, and its result count is requested_count. Returns each creator's handle, followers and latest post. Instagram creators also come with bio and links; TikTok creators say not_read, and instagram_profile reads Instagram accounts only. Price: charged what each scan read cost, never above its line. Usually a few minutes; until it is done the reply says collecting, and a repeat call returns what it found.

instagram_post.description: Takes post_urls, and needs no brief or keywords. Returns the creator of each post, with the handle, post link and caption. It reads no bio or links, so bio_status says not_read; instagram_profile reads them, charged as its own source. Price: charged what the read cost, never above the line for the links sent. Usually a minute or two, in the background.

post_urls.description: Instagram post or reel links to read.

instagram_profile.description: Takes handles, and needs no brief or keywords. Returns each creator's handle, bio, links and latest posts, with the address the bio holds in contact_email. It also works for a creator the campaign already shows, and that row says already_on_list. Price: charged what the read cost, never above the line for the handles sent. Usually a minute or two, in the background.

meta.description: Takes keywords and countries. Returns each creator's handle and the marketplace facts it states. Price: charges nothing. Usually under a minute, inside this call.

tiktok_keyword.description: Takes search_queries, hashtags, profiles, video_urls, date_from, date_to and region, or the keywords when no list is sent. Returns each creator's handle, bio, links, video links and captions, with the address the bio holds in contact_email. Price: charged per creator requested, once it finds any creator. Usually 1 to 4 minutes, in the background.

date_from.description: Oldest post date to read, as YYYY-MM-DD.

date_to.description: Newest post date to read, as YYYY-MM-DD.

region.description: A two-letter country code. It reads TikTok as seen from that country and does not filter results.

web.description: Takes the brief and categories. Returns each creator's handle and followers. Price: charged per search and per profile read, never above its line. Usually under a minute, inside this call.

tiktok_shop_filters.description: TikTok Shop campaigns only: the brief and Learned Facts as TikTok Shop's creator filters, on every search.

category_pro.description: Category Pro, e.g. Health and Wellness.

left_to_review.description: Brief parts no filter carries, e.g. tone or no deal accounts.
